![](week-08_files/figure-revealjs/dat-length-1.png){fig-align='center' width=672} ::: ::: ## Realisation and length ::: {.cell layout-align="center" output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} dative <- dative |> mutate( Realisation_num = ifelse(RealizationOfRecipient == "NP", 0, 1) ) dative |> ggplot(aes(LengthOfRecipient, Realisation_num)) + geom_smooth( method = "glm", method.args = list(family = "binomial"), colour = "sienna" ) + ylim(0, 1) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week-08_files/figure-revealjs/dat-real-length-1.png){fig-align='center' width=672} ::: ::: ## Regression model ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} dat_bm <- brm( RealizationOfRecipient ~ LengthOfRecipient, family = "bernoulli", data = dative, seed = 3926, file = "cache/dat_bm" ) summary(dat_bm) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Family: bernoulli Links: mu = logit Formula: RealizationOfRecipient ~ LengthOfRecipient Data: dative (Number of observations: 3263) Draws: 4 chains, each with iter = 2000; warmup = 1000; thin = 1; total post-warmup draws = 4000 Regression Coefficients: Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Rhat Bulk_ESS Tail_ESS Intercept -2.35 0.08 -2.50 -2.19 1.00 3725 2796 LengthOfRecipient 0.70 0.04 0.63 0.78 1.00 3301 2502 Draws were sampled using sampling(NUTS). For each parameter, Bulk_ESS and Tail_ESS are effective sample size measures, and Rhat is the potential scale reduction factor on split chains (at convergence, Rhat = 1). ``` ::: ::: ## Posterior distributions ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week-08_files/figure-revealjs/dat-bm-dens-1.png){fig-align='center' width=672} ::: ::: ## Odd ratio of the effect of length ::: {.cell layout-align="center" output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code} dat_bm_draws <- as_draws_df(dat_bm) |> mutate( Length_OR = exp(b_LengthOfRecipient) ) dat_bm_draws |> ggplot(aes(Length_OR)) + geom_density(fill = "aquamarine4", alpha = 0.5) + labs(x = "Odd ratio of the effect of recipient length") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week-08_files/figure-revealjs/dat-bm-draws-1.png){fig-align='center' width=672} ::: ::: . . . ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} | 90% | 80% | 70% | 60% | 40% | |:-----------:|:------------:|:-----------:|:------------:|:------------:| | [1.9, 2.15] | [1.92, 2.12] | [1.94, 2.1] | [1.95, 2.09] | [1.98, 2.06] | ::: ::: ## From 1 to 2 to 3 words ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} dat_bm_draws <- dat_bm_draws |> mutate( p_1 = plogis(b_Intercept + b_LengthOfRecipient), p_2 = plogis(b_Intercept + b_LengthOfRecipient * 2), p_3 = plogis(b_Intercept + b_LengthOfRecipient * 3), p_2_1 = p_2 - p_1, p_3_2 = p_3 - p_2, ) quantile2(dat_bm_draws$p_2_1, probs = c(0.05, 0.95)) |> round(2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` q5 q95 0.11 0.13 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} quantile2(dat_bm_draws$p_3_2, probs = c(0.05, 0.95)) |> round(2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` q5 q95 0.14 0.18 ``` ::: ::: ## Expected values ::: {.cell layout-align="center" output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidybayes) pred_grid <- tibble( LengthOfRecipient = seq( min(dative$LengthOfRecipient), max(dative$LengthOfRecipient) ) ) dat_bm_epred <- epred_draws(dat_bm, pred_grid) |> mutate( median = median(.epred), lower = quantile2(.epred, probs = 0.025), upper = quantile2(.epred, probs = 0.975) ) dat_bm_epred |> ggplot(aes(LengthOfRecipient, median)) + geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.2) + geom_line(linewidth = 1, colour = "sienna") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week-08_files/figure-revealjs/dat-bm-epred-1.png){fig-align='center' width=672} ::: ::: ## Results ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"} - At 90% confidence, the probability of the recipient being realised as PP increases by a factor of 1.9 to 2.15 for each extra word in the recipient. - The probability of a PP increases by 11-13 percentage points from 1 to 2 words, at 90% probability. (But it is still below 50%, so an NP is still more likely). - Above 10 words, an PP is virtually certain. :::

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
